The name practically says so, and React's own reference defines Client Components as components "rendered on the client". Server Components really can't use state or event handlers, so "client" reads like "the browser and nothing else". And before Server Components, "client-side rendering" meant exactly that: an empty page that JavaScript fills in. The half that's true: a Client Component's code is sent to the browser, and only there can it become interactive. What's missing is that the browser may not be the only place it renders.
An app with Server Components can involve two server-side steps, and they do different things.

The first is the Server Components environment. React's reference describes Server Components as rendering ahead of time, before bundling, "in an environment separate from your client app or SSR server", either once at build time or for each request. While rendering there, React runs only Server Components. When it reaches a component imported from a client module, it doesn't run it; it leaves that part of the tree, with its props, for the client to render. Server Components never run in the browser, and their code is never shipped there.
. React's docs say the combined result "can then be server-side rendered (SSR) to create the initial HTML for the page". That pass renders the whole tree to HTML, Client Components included, just as
always has. In the browser, React then

that HTML: it renders the Client Components again, adopts the existing DOM and attaches event handlers. So on a server-rendered page, one Client Component can render twice per load: once on the server for HTML, once in the browser to hydrate.
'use client' marks a module boundary, not a runtime

The directive goes at the very top of a file and marks that module and its transitive dependencies as client code. When a Server Component imports such a file, compatible bundlers treat the import as the boundary between server-run and client-run code. It answers "which code must be bundled and sent to the browser?", not "where does this render?".
The boundary lives in the module graph, not the render tree. A Server Component passed as

to a Client Component stays a Server Component: it has already rendered by the time the Client Component runs. And everything crossing the boundary as props must be serializable, so plain data, JSX and promises work, but ordinary functions and class instances don't.
